title: DuET: Dual-View Tensor-to-Topology Spectral Adapter for Enhancing Sparse Tensor Factorization

problem.claim: Tensor factorization estimates unobserved entries from sparse tensors using latent representations and a predictor.

gap.claim: Under extreme sparsity, entities with few interactions develop noisy, undertrained latent vectors that generalize poorly.

contributions.claim: DuET is a model-agnostic refinement framework that stabilizes tensor-factorization embeddings by separating structural denoising from tensor factorization.
DuET distills a dual-view structural prior and refines it using per-view low-rank spectral filtering and mode-wise gated residual refinement.
The refinement is theoretically guaranteed to be Frobenius-norm non-expansive.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on nine real-world tensors report consistent improvements for retrieval and completion.
The reported gains reach up to 52.1% in NDCG@10.
The reported RMSE reductions reach up to 13.8%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sparse tensors occur in real-world datasets, and tensor factorization is used to estimate unobserved entries.
Extreme sparsity produces noisy, undertrained latent vectors with poor generalization.
DuET separates structural denoising from tensor factorization and applies dual-view spectral and gated residual refinement.
The refinement is Frobenius-norm non-expansive, supporting stability under repeated refinement.
The framework integrates with existing tensor-factorization models and reports improvements across nine real-world tensors.

source_observation.claim: The framework separates structural denoising from tensor factorization and refines embeddings using structural priors.

interpretation.claim: Separating structural refinement from the task model may help address representation noise caused by extreme sparsity.

application.claim: For sparse higher-order data, consider adding a model-agnostic structural refinement stage before or alongside prediction.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach benefits sparse settings beyond the reported tensor-factorization tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the nine datasets, tensor dimensions, sparsity levels, baselines, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not provide the assumptions or proof details for the non-expansive guarantee.
The abstract does not report statistical significance, variance, or computational overhead.
